newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Spain Treasury bills to fall slightly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spain Treasury bills to fall slightly.

text.p: Spain's one-year and 18-month bill yields are expected to fall to new record lows at around five percent at an auction on Wednesday, money market dealers said on Tuesday.
"The Treasury should sell at around market levels. We could have a marginal rate at around 5.00/01 percent for the one-year and at 5.01/02 pct for 18-month bills," a dealer said.
On the grey market, the two maturities were trading earlier at around five percent.
Dealers said the yield could even be a bit lower, although the final result will be affected by the amount of the two issues.
On May 13, one-year bills were allotted with yield at 5.087 percent, while the 18-month yield was 5.109 percent.
Traders added that demand is not expected to top the one the Treasury received two weeks ago, with a likely joint demand of around 650 billion pesetas for the two maturities.
On May 13 the joint volume of demand was above one trillion pesetas.
"I expect a change also in the sense it seems to me people would ask more for one-year bills than for 18-month bills," a trader said.
Since the Spanish Treasury started offering 18-month bills one month ago, dealers have been looking more to the longer maturity.
"This (lower expected demand) for 18-month-bills has something to do with the French election and with the fact people started to be more cautious," a trader explained.
"They prefer to wait for the second round of the French election before increasing their position in assets longer than a year," a dealer said.

But others stressed the fact that after the Bank of Spain had cut its official rate 12 times in 17 months, the market is starting to consider the possibility that the interest rate downtrend could reach an end.
"They can't go on for ever, cutting the key money market rate once a month," a dealer said.
On Friday, the Treasury will have to pay back old maturing bills for 373.24 billion pesetas.
One-year bill yield hit its record low on January 22 at 5.052 percent, while the record low for 18-month bills was on May 13.
